problem: Foundation-model robot systems map model outputs directly to actions or use monolithic pipelines, are tied to a specific embodiment, and lack persistent, multi-modal, auditable memory. Existing embodied benchmarks are fragmented (indoor vs outdoor), single-skill and static.
motivation: Physical execution has partial observability, actuation uncertainty and no explicit completion signals, so LLM agents drift or terminate prematurely. Long-term interaction needs memory that binds dialogue, egocentric vision, identities, places, time and provenance, and that can improve from its own failures.
key_idea: A robot Agent OS layer above VLMs and low-level controllers that combines a reasoning-execution-verification harness (main LLM, Skill Runner, multi-stage Verifier), a typed source-grounded multi-modal graph memory with failure-driven gated self-evolution, and a new executable benchmark (EmbodiedWorldBench).
insight: On the EmbodiedWorldBench subset, the same Qwen3.6-Plus controller gains about 12 points TSR when the hierarchical harness with verification replaces plain ReAct, and a stronger main LLM helps further. For memory, graph seed-and-expand retrieval beats snippet-based memory, and gated evo-assets give small, consistent gains on later splits. The appendix shows candidate-level wins often fail stack confirmation (only 1 of 8 splits promoted an asset), so conservative gating matters.
method: Agent Harness: main LLM does scene-conditioned planning with memory and context, delegates multi-step subtasks to a Skill Runner (isolated local context, returns compressed outcome), and receives Verifier feedback
Multi-stage Verifier: runtime (stagnation/loops/collisions), skill-level (semantic subgoal check) and finish-time verification before termination is allowed

Edge-cloud routing and memory: a Tiny LLM on the edge escalates to a cloud Large LLM via a learned router; private edge memory vs shared cloud common memory with a privacy gate (>99% classification accuracy reported)

Typed graph memory: nodes for sources, evidence, entities, places, sessions and events; temporal/spatial/identity/provenance edges; selective writing with merging and superseding; hybrid seed scoring (semantic+lexical+metadata+type) then typed-edge subgraph expansion with retrieval traces
Failure-driven lifelong self-evolution: Diagnose→Propose→Compile (JSON DSL evo-assets)→Gate (target gain ≥τ_gain, regression ≤τ_reg); assets promoted only to later splits (no leakage)
EmbodiedWorldBench: 16 UnrealZoo scenes (indoor/outdoor/hybrid), 200+ tasks in 4 difficulty levels, LLM-generated, human-refined queries, visibility isolation, and trace-grounded TSR/GCR scoring

Small-model training pipeline: text sandbox environments, teacher trajectory distillation with an LLM-judge filter, SFT, then RL with GiGPO and a self-evolving LLM-as-a-Judge reward engine with a Meta-Judge (human alignment ~60% to >90%)

setting.backbone: Agent eval: Qwen3.6-Plus or DeepSeek-V4-Pro as main LLM (frozen), Qwen3-VL-Plus as observation tool; memory: Qwen3.6-Plus / GPT-5.4 / Qwen3.5-Flash writer and answerer (frozen)
setting.training_data: Agent and memory evaluations are training-free with frozen API LLMs; the separate small-model pipeline uses private synthetic sandbox trajectories (no results released)
setting.observation: Text/semantic-map input plus VLM-generated textual observation evidence from first-person views; memory experiments use dialogue, images, video frames and egocentric video
setting.action_space: High-level tool/skill calls (NavMesh-based navigation commands, observe, NPC dialogue, report)
setting.simulator: UnrealZoo (Unreal Engine 5) for the agent benchmark; text-based sandbox for training
setting.privileged: Filtered semantic map is given to the agent by design; hidden evaluator states are isolated. Self-evolution uses ground-truth answers post hoc on completed splits.

numbers_note: Self-evolution gains are given in a figure and in text only (NExT-QA +4.1 Acc@All, LoCoMo +1.2, OpenEQA +1.2, Mem-Gallery +0.4, EgoLife 65.4→66.2). No standard navigation benchmark (R2R, ObjectNav etc.) is evaluated. The agent-benchmark subset is not described in detail.
results: With Qwen3.6-Plus, the ABot-AgentOS harness raises TSR/GCR from 49.97/57.95 (ReAct) to 61.96/68.79 on an EmbodiedWorldBench subset, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro reaches 68.18/74.62. The static graph memory gets 87.5 on LoCoMo (vs Mem0 85.6, human 87.9), 76.5 on NExT-QA (vs GraphVideoAgent 73.3) and 65.4 avg on EgoLifeQA (vs EGAgent 57.5). On OpenEQA (59.9) it beats listed memory baselines but stays below direct VQA with the same frames (74.1 for GPT-5.4).
limitations: Agent evaluation is on a small, unspecified benchmark subset with simulator-only, NavMesh-abstracted control; there is no real-robot validation, and the benchmark is not yet released

Memory baselines are partly reproduced or taken from other protocols, so comparisons are not fully controlled; on OpenEQA, direct VQA outperforms the memory system; self-evolution gains are small and need ground-truth or post-hoc feedback

Failures remain in perception feedback: the VLM tool confuses people and objects, and the agent confuses visible regions with its own location; the training pipeline results and router are not reported
